description: Henri Polaklaan 16-28 (BAG 1838-1905, one row): 5.3 m brick fronts with a raised ground storey (door on the left axis, two windows, stoop), two upper storeys and a pointed brick gable with one arched light; three axes of white-framed windows with a top light, iron wall anchors, white sills; one house in the row (Polaklaan 20) has a plain cornice instead of the gable

match.note: Polaklaan 16-28: BAG dates 1838-1905 on one row; 3DBAG eaves 12.1-12.5, ridge 14.8-15.6; keyed by eaves and the face pin

point-gable.note: a pointed brick gable, rakes from the cornice at 12.3 m to the apex at 14.2 m, one arched light about 1.3 m tall (crownRise is in upper-storey heights: 0.58 x 3.4 m = 1.9 m)

plain-cornice.note: Polaklaan 20: no gable, plain cornice at 12.3 m

door-left.note: raised ground storey, double door with a transom on the left axis, two windows, stoop (all houses of the row in the 2024-12-10 strip)

rhythm.groundFloor: raised, double door and two windows
schemaLimits: the sculpted keystone heads of 44 are plain blocks
the dormer's low side cheeks are not drawn

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2024-12-10 gridded 80 px/m (street level at strip bottom): parterre windows 1.85-4.5 m, storey 1 5.5-8.2, storey 2 8.9-11.4; eaves 12.3-12.4; gable apex 14.2-14.3, arched light 12.3-13.8; 5.3 m fronts

schemaLimits: the stoop is the library stoop; the white outer false gable above the brick one is not drawn
the gable light is round-headed, the photo has a pointed Gothic head
